name: Palestinian Territories
summary_text: The Palestinian Territories are dangerous for trans visitors, with a hard internal split. In the West Bank, same-sex conduct is not criminalised (1951 Jordanian code) but there are no protections, family/clan hostility is severe, and LGBT Palestinians flee to Israel for safety (Israeli courts now grant such asylum claims). In Gaza, a British Mandate law technically allows 10 years, Hamas has executed people for alleged homosexuality, and the territory is in a catastrophic war. Cairo 52 notes trans identities are not explicitly criminalised but gender-affirming healthcare is essentially destroyed/unavailable.

sources.title: Palestinian Territories (West Bank and Gaza) | Cairo 52 Legal Research Institute
sources.claim_summary: Cairo 52 country review of the Palestinian Territories: Gaza and the West Bank have distinct penal codes; trans identities not explicitly criminalised in either; homosexuality laws seldom enforced; gender-affirming healthcare severely limited (destruction of hospitals in Gaza, occupation); no clear legal gender recognition due to multiple jurisdictions; Israel's portrayal as a safe haven for LGBTQ+ Palestinians criticised as pinkwashing.

sources.title: LGBTQ Rights in Palestine: West Bank, Gaza, and Asylum - LegalClarity
sources.claim_summary: LegalClarity overview (June 2026): no unified legal code - the West Bank (Jordanian Penal Code 1960) does not criminalise same-sex conduct, while Gaza retains a British colonial-era law punishing it with up to 10 years; neither territory offers anti-discrimination protections, relationship recognition or a gender-transition pathway; social and family-level persecution poses risks independent of statute.

sources.title: LGBTQ rights in Palestine - Wikipedia
sources.claim_summary: Wikipedia overview: mixed legality - West Bank legal since 1951 with equal age of consent; Gaza unclear; sections on civil rights and violence, health, the Israeli-Palestinian conflict (including alleged blackmailing by the Israeli military), and LGBTQ activism (Aswat).

sources.title: Audacity in Adversity: LGBT Activism in the Middle East and North Africa | HRW
sources.claim_summary: HRW report (April 2018) 'Audacity in Adversity': LGBT activism in the Middle East and North Africa - covers Palestinian territories, including the work of al-Qaws and the legal situation under both Palestinian Authority and Hamas governance.

Times of Israel: rights groups slammed Palestinian police for banning LGBTQ activity - after the police action against al-Qaws, the foundation received a wave of hate messages which activists said 'pose a serious threat' to the gay community.

sources.title: Human Rights Watch, Women’s Centre for Legal Aid and Counselling, and Equality Now, Joint Submission to the CEDAW Committee on the State of Palestine, 70th session | Human Rights W
sources.claim_summary: HRW + Women's Centre for Legal Aid and Counselling + Equality Now joint statement (June 2018): on Palestinian women's rights and legal protections - context for the broader rights environment in the Palestinian territories.

Times of Israel: Israel to allow LGBT Palestinians granted temporary asylum to work - some 90 LGBT Palestinians have received temporary permits to seek refuge in Israel after fleeing violence in the territories.
